title: Challenge: Queue from Two Stacks

writing.exampleCaption: Complete std-only queue-with-stacks program for its typed teaching fixture. Parsing and output construction are separate from the core algorithm.
writing.explanation:
Reversing a whole batch restores FIFO order without disturbing older items. The worked program demonstrates this invariant on an independent fixture, so you can study the implementation before predicting the challenge result.

For teaching input `enqueue1 enqueue2 dequeue front`, the worked program returns `2`. Its functions are complete and use only std. Adapt the same state transitions to the visible challenge input `enqueue3 enqueue5 enqueue8 dequeue dequeue enqueue2 front`; predict that result before opening the answer reveal. The precise contract is: Execute the space-separated queue operations and return the value produced by front.

Return canonical output: lowercase booleans, decimal integers without leading zeros, comma-separated values and semicolon-separated groups, with no extra whitespace or final newline. Whole medians use integer form and half medians use .5. Textual sentinels such as none and # retain their stated meaning. String and character-grid fixtures use ASCII unless the lesson explicitly specifies Unicode scalar values.

Solve the exact task, not just the visible example: Execute the space-separated queue operations and return the value produced by front. On input `enqueue3 enqueue5 enqueue8 dequeue dequeue enqueue2 front`, predict the output before opening the answer reveal. The revealed output is a test oracle for this case, while private checks exercise other legal cases. Start by stating the input grammar and output format in your own words. Parse the complete input, including surrounding whitespace, before relying on any convenient positions in the example.

Build the solution around one maintained claim: Reverse the input stack into an output stack only when the output side is empty. Decide what state represents that claim, how it is initialized, what a single update does, and when the algorithm stops. A stack remembers unfinished work in last-in-first-out order; a queue processes work in first-in-first-out order. Say what each stored item still needs. Trace the visible input by hand and record at least two intermediate states, not only the final answer. If the trace cannot justify your predicted output, there is a gap between the idea and the implementation.

Check both correctness and cost. The intended bound is O(1) amortised operation · O(n) space; explain which operation dominates it and how many times the input can trigger that operation. Check empty containers, one item, repeated equal values, and the work left in the structure after the input ends. Add one small case that should succeed, one boundary case, and one case chosen to challenge the invariant. Compare your hand result with the program's result, then use a failing case to fix the earliest incorrect state transition rather than patching the final output.
writing.feedback: For this input the result is `5`. Reversing a whole batch restores FIFO order without disturbing older items. Compare this independent fixture with the worked trace: Enqueue 3,5,8 into incoming. Its transfer produces outgoing top 3; two dequeues remove 3 and 5. Enqueuing 2 remains in incoming while outgoing top 8 is still the correct front.
